Identify its physical support from the supplied frozen entities, if identifiable; otherwise null. support_verified means original pixels support this support relation in at least two different supplied frames. Do not invent invisible floor/wall nodes. A contained plant can have its pot as support; nearby furniture is not automatically support. Keep ambiguity.
2. For EVERY supplied reference frame and EVERY unordered pair of target entities whose VERIFIED support_entity_id equals that reference's origin_anchor_id, return THREE relations, one for each axis. The reference is explicitly defined in this shot's 3D coordinates: origin = center of the origin anchor; v = normalized horizontal vector from origin to reference anchor; z = supplied physical up; u = v cross z. Axes are cross_anchor_up=u, toward_reference=v, vertical=z. Matrices/anchor geometry are supplied. This is a right-handed physical reference, NOT image left/right and NOT camera near/far. For each ordered endpoint pair i,j, the relation is the SIGN of (center_i - center_j) dot axis. Negative means the first center is on the negative side relative to the second, positive vice versa. Camera projection can reverse image ordering without reversing this physical sign.

The measured thing is OBB-center order, NOT full bounding-box/footprint separation. Partial overlap does not by itself make center order unknowable. Conversely an occluding surface is not automatically the object's center: use visible body/rim/base geometry and known-up projection with the supplied 3D size/depth evidence, and explicitly consider whether plausible center error could reverse the order. Do not fabricate a hidden contact point or tight depth bounds. A support-center interpretation may corroborate centers when the objects are upright; state the assumption.

Independently inspect the originals to assess the reference direction and support. For determinate orders provide >=2 distinct-frame witnesses, original-pixel regions for each object and the supporting/reference context, with a concrete account of depth/occlusion and how it corresponds to the defined physical axis. You may use several temporal views, but repeated frames are correlated. If the original evidence cannot distinguish the center order or cannot connect the reference direction to the scene, output unknown and geometry_error_can_reverse=true. A matching raw 3D sign alone is not enough.
